docs.title: Protodex
docs.text:
Protodex is an open-source (Apache-2.0), self-hostable Protobuf schema registry that is wire-compatible with the public bufbuild/registry-proto API, so the stock buf CLI can push to and pull from it.

It is an independent clean-room implementation, not affiliated with or endorsed by Buf Technologies, Inc.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
• Quickstart: run Protodex with Docker Compose or Helm and push your first module.
  • Migrating from buf.build: move an existing repository (hosts, buf.lock, plugins) and use protodex migrate-buf.
  • Configuration, Operations (backup, restore, upgrades) and Security.
  • buf CLI compatibility: the tested version matrix.
  • FAQ and non-goals.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Protodex is early software. Check the compatibility matrix and the roadmap for what is implemented.

docs.title: Branch protection for main
docs.text:
Policy:

  • No direct pushes; all changes land via pull request.
  • At least 1 approving review, including a CODEOWNER; stale approvals are dismissed on new commits.
  • Branch must be up to date and all required checks must pass: build-test, docs, lint, generated, licenses, proto, docker, helm, security, dependency-review, dco, pr-title (described in CONTRIBUTING.md).
  • No force pushes or branch deletion. Administrators are included.
  • Squash merge only, so the Conventional Commits PR title becomes the commit message.

Notes:

  • dependency-review runs on public repositories. For private repositories, enable the dependency graph and GitHub Advanced Security, then set the DEPENDENCY_REVIEW_ENABLED Actions variable to true; otherwise the job is skipped. The licenses and security checks still run.
  • gitleaks-action needs a GITLEAKS_LICENSE secret only if the repository belongs to an organization. Personal-account repositories do not.
  • A check only becomes selectable as "required" after it has run once, so apply this after the first CI run on a PR.

docs.title: Applying it
docs.text:
A repository admin can apply the policy with the GitHub CLI:

gh api -X PUT repos/marijnkoesen/protodex/branches/main/protection \
  -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" --input - <<'JSON'
{
  "required_status_checks": {
    "strict": true,
    "checks": [
      {"context": "build-test"}, {"context": "docs"}, {"context": "lint"}, {"context": "generated"},
      {"context": "licenses"}, {"context": "proto"}, {"context": "docker"},
      {"context": "helm"}, {"context": "security"},
      {"context": "dependency-review"}, {"context": "dco"},
      {"context": "pr-title"}
    ]
  },
  "enforce_admins": true,
  "required_pull_request_reviews": {
    "required_approving_review_count": 1,
    "require_code_owner_reviews": true,
    "dismiss_stale_reviews": true
  },
  "restrictions": null,
  "allow_force_pushes": false,
  "allow_deletions": false,
  "required_conversation_resolution": true
}
JSON

gh api -X PATCH repos/marijnkoesen/protodex \
  -f allow_squash_merge=true -f allow_merge_commit=false -f allow_rebase_merge=false

docs.title: buf CLI compatibility
docs.text: Protodex is tested against released buf CLI binaries by the conformance suite in test/conformance. Each scenario starts a fresh protodex (ephemeral store + filesystem blob store, a bootstrapped admin token, organization acme) over TLS and drives the real CLI.

docs.title: Matrix
docs.text:
The suite trusts its ephemeral TLS certificate via SSL_CERT_FILE, which Go binaries on macOS ignore (older buf releases). Run it on Linux; macOS is not supported by the harness.

Result of the full matrix on the SQLite backend (2026-11-17, linux/amd64, make conformance CONFORMANCE_VERSIONS=all):

backend buf login module organization push labels dep-update build export lint breaking generate sqlite 1.32.2 pass n/a n/a pass n/a pass pass pass pass pass pass sqlite 1.35.1 pass n/a n/a pass n/a pass pass pass pass pass pass sqlite 1.40.1 pass pass pass pass pass pass pass pass pass pass pass sqlite 1.45.0 pass pass pass pass pass pass pass pass pass pass pass sqlite 1.50.1 pass pass pass pass pass pass pass pass pass pass pass sqlite 1.55.1 pass pass pass pass pass pass pass pass pass pass pass sqlite 1.57.2 pass pass pass pass pass pass pass pass pass pass pass sqlite 1.60.0 pass pass pass pass pass pass pass pass pass pass pass sqlite 1.65.0 pass pass pass pass pass pass pass pass pass pass pass sqlite 1.70.0 pass pass pass pass pass pass pass pass pass pass pass sqlite 1.75.0 pass pass pass pass pass pass pass pass pass pass pass

n/a: the CLI version has no such command (buf registry module ..., buf registry organization ... and label commands arrived in the 1.40 line). On those versions the other scenarios create modules directly in the store instead.

Minimum supported version: 1.32.2 (the first CLI line with v2 buf.yaml and the buf.registry.*.v1 API protodex implements). Older CLIs speak the v1alpha1 registry API and are not supported. The latest tested release is 1.75.0. The nightly CI run refreshes this matrix; update the table from its job summaries when it changes.

docs.title: Scenarios
docs.text:
Scenario What the CLI does login unauthenticated push is refused; registry login --token-stdin writes .netrc; registry whoami (where available); push with the stored credentials; registry logout; push refused again module registry module create / info --format=json / duplicate create (already exists) / settings update (or update) / deprecate / undeprecate / delete organization registry organization create / duplicate create and clash with an existing owner fail / info --format=json / update --description --url / delete is refused while the organization owns a module, then works push push, idempotent re-push, --label, changed content → new commit, commit info, push to a missing module fails labels label list, info, archive (hidden from list, shown with --archive-status=archived), default label cannot be archived, unarchive dep-update dep update writes commit + b5 digest to buf.lock; a new upstream commit is picked up; build from a cold cache; push records the dep; remote build includes it build build of a remote module by name, :main, :label and :commit gives identical images; unknown label / module fail; local workspace with remote dep builds from a cold cache export export by name and commit; exporting a dependent module includes its dependency; missing module fails lint local module importing a remote module with a lint violation lints clean (deps are not linted); a local violation is reported; buf lint <remote> reports the remote violation breaking breaking --against <remote> passes for unchanged content and reports a deleted field generate buf generate with a local plugin (protoc-gen-conformance, built from this repo): local files only by default, remote dependency with --include-imports, and a remote module as input

Each scenario adapts to the CLI by probing buf <command> --help, not by hard-coded version ranges, except the lint category: STANDARD from 1.40, DEFAULT before.

docs.title: buf registry command support
docs.text:
Every buf registry subcommand that talks to the registry API, as of buf 1.75.0:

Command Status login, logout, whoami supported (login, whoami scenarios) module create, info, update / settings update, deprecate, undeprecate, delete supported (module scenario) module label list, info, archive, unarchive supported (labels scenario) module commit info supported (push scenario) module commit list, resolve, add-label served by implemented RPCs (ListCommits, GetCommits, CreateOrUpdateLabels) but not covered by a scenario yet organization create, info, update (--description, --url), delete supported (organization scenario). Instance admins only. delete is refused while the organization owns modules, and for mirror owners plugin ..., policy ..., sdk ... not supported: protodex implements no plugin, policy or generated-SDK services; the CLI gets unimplemented cc local only (clears the CLI cache)

There is no buf registry user or member command: users are provisioned by an instance admin (UserService.CreateUsers / DeleteUsers, or protodex owner) or through OIDC, and organization membership and organization settings (GetOrganizationSettings, UpdateOrganizationSettings) are not modeled (see owners.md).

docs.title: Running it
docs.text:
make conformance                                   # PR subset: 1.32.2, 1.57.2, 1.75.0
make conformance CONFORMANCE_VERSIONS=all          # full matrix
make conformance CONFORMANCE_VERSIONS=1.60.0       # one version
PROTODEX_CONFORMANCE_BUF=/usr/local/bin/buf go test ./test/conformance/   # your own binary

Without any of these settings the suite uses PROTODEX_TEST_BUF or buf on PATH, and skips if neither exists, so go test ./... never needs the network. Settings (see also the package doc):

Variable Meaning PROTODEX_CONFORMANCE_BUF_VERSIONS pr, all or 1.57.2,1.75.0: download those releases PROTODEX_CONFORMANCE_BUF comma-separated buf binaries to test PROTODEX_CONFORMANCE_BACKENDS store backends to run (default: all registered) PROTODEX_CONFORMANCE_REPORT write the Markdown result table to this file PROTODEX_CONFORMANCE_FAULT digest: inject a server bug (the suite must fail) PROTODEX_CONFORMANCE_CACHE download cache (default <user cache dir>/protodex/buf)

Test names are TestConformance/<backend>/buf-<version>/<scenario>, so -run 'TestConformance/sqlite/buf-1.75.0/push' selects one cell.

docs.title: Downloads are checksum-verified
docs.text:
go run ./test/conformance/cmd/fetchbuf get 1.75.0 (used by the suite) downloads buf-<OS>-<arch> from the GitHub release and refuses it unless its SHA-256 matches bufdl/checksums.txt, which is committed. To add a release:

  1. go run ./test/conformance/cmd/fetchbuf pin 1.76.0 (records the release's published sha256.txt entries for Linux/macOS, x86_64/arm64).
  2. Add the version to bufdl/versions.txt (mark it pr if it becomes the latest; move the marker off the old one).
  3. make conformance CONFORMANCE_VERSIONS=1.76.0, then update the table above.

docs.title: Failure output
docs.text: On failure the test prints the CLI command, its stdout and stderr, and the server's request log for that scenario: every buf invocation interleaved with the access log (procedure, Connect code, duration) and the bodies of error responses.

docs.title: Generated-code compatibility of mirrors
docs.text:
test/conformance/gencompat_test.go checks that the mirrored modules (see mirror.md) are transparent: it imports the googleapis/googleapis and bufbuild/protovalidate pins of mirror.yaml into protodex, then runs buf generate --include-imports for a fixture module (test/conformance/testdata/gencompat) once against the mirrored modules and once against clones of the upstream repositories at the same pins. The Go (protoc-gen-go, protoc-gen-go-grpc) and TypeScript (protoc-gen-es) output must be identical apart from generator/compiler version header lines, and every mirrored .proto must equal upstream (path and bytes, so go_package and all options). Plugins are local and pinned (protoc-gen-go follows go.mod; the others are constants in the test).

It needs the network, so it runs only with PROTODEX_CONFORMANCE_GENCOMPAT=1 (the generated-code compatibility job of the conformance workflow). PROTODEX_CONFORMANCE_GENCOMPAT_FAULT=go_package makes the mirror alter a go_package; the test must then fail, and the workflow checks that it does. The test mirrors a small self-contained subset of googleapis (the whole tree does not build as one module because google/cloud/* imports protos that are not in the repository).

docs.title: Store backends
docs.text: The suite is parametrised by metadata store backend (backend_test.go). SQLite is the only one today. A new backend (Postgres, #23) registers a Backend from an init function in test/conformance/backend_<name>_test.go, with a Skip func that opts out when its database is not configured (for example no DSN in the environment), and the whole matrix runs against it as TestConformance/<name>/....

docs.title: Catching digest bugs
docs.text:
TestDigestFaultIsCaught runs the dep-update and build scenarios with a deliberate digest bug: the server stores correct data but sends every module digest (in Upload, GetCommits, GetGraph, Download responses) with its last byte changed. It passes only if those scenarios fail because of the digest; the CLI reports Digest verification failed ... Expected digest (from buf.lock) ... Actual digest .... This runs on every suite run. To see the whole matrix go red by hand:

PROTODEX_CONFORMANCE_FAULT=digest make conformance CONFORMANCE_VERSIONS=1.57.2

(verified 2026-11-17 with buf 1.57.2: dep-update, build, export, lint, breaking and generate fail; login, module, push and labels do not read digests back and pass.)

docs.title: Golden fixtures
docs.text: The traffic-capture harness (test/capture, #3) has not produced committed fixtures yet (docs/behavior-spec/rpc-matrix.md is unpopulated and there is no test/fixtures/), so the suite checks behaviour end to end instead of comparing RPC traffic against recordings. Once fixtures exist, they can be asserted from the request log the harness already keeps.

docs.title: Observed CLI behaviour
docs.text:
• buf push --label=X moves only X, not the default label; the first push without --label sets the default label.
  • buf registry login <host:port> --token-stdin writes an entry for the host (without the port) to $HOME/.netrc, which later commands use when BUF_TOKEN is unset.
  • The CLI verifies downloaded module content against the b5 digest the server reported, so a wrong digest fails dep update and build with Digest verification failed, and with them every scenario that reads a pushed module back.
  • buf registry label ... (1.40 line) became buf registry module label ... later; the old path still exists, hidden, in 1.57.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Settings are layered; later wins: built-in defaults, JSON config file (-config / PROTODEX_CONFIG), PROTODEX_* environment variables, flags of protodex serve. Unknown JSON keys are rejected.

Key Env Default Description addr PROTODEX_ADDR :8080 Listen address (h2c; terminate TLS at a proxy). log_level PROTODEX_LOG_LEVEL info debug, info, warn, error. log_format PROTODEX_LOG_FORMAT text text or json. max_request_bytes PROTODEX_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES 64 MiB Upper bound for a request body. db_path PROTODEX_DB_PATH SQLite database. Required for registry RPCs. Holds an exclusive lock: one server per database. blob_dir PROTODEX_BLOB_DIR <db_path>.blobs Blob directory (filesystem backend). max_push_files, max_push_file_bytes, max_push_bytes PROTODEX_MAX_PUSH_BYTES 5000 / 10 MiB / 64 MiB Push limits, see push. rate_limit.* PROTODEX_RATE_LIMIT_* 50/s per IP, 100/s per token Rate limiting; 0 disables. trust_forwarded_for only behind a trusted proxy. gc_interval, gc_grace_period, gc_dry_run PROTODEX_GC_* 1h, 24h, false See garbage collection. shutdown_timeout PROTODEX_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT 30s Grace for in-flight requests on SIGTERM. tracing_enabled, otlp_endpoint PROTODEX_TRACING_ENABLED, PROTODEX_OTLP_ENDPOINT off OpenTelemetry tracing, see observability. oidc.* PROTODEX_OIDC_* off Single sign-on; see the README and permissions. The client secret is env-only.

The authoritative list is internal/config/config.go; the compose and Helm settings are in the deploy/ READMEs.

docs.title: CLI commands
docs.text: Command Purpose protodex serve Run the server. protodex bootstrap Create the first admin, instance organization and mirror owners; prints the first token once. protodex migrate [up\|down] Apply or roll back database migrations. Run after upgrading. protodex owner, protodex contributor Manage users, organizations, roles and per-module grants (owners). protodex mirror Import upstream modules (mirroring). protodex migrate-buf Rewrite a repository's buf.yaml hosts (migration).

docs.title: FAQ and non-goals
docs.text:
Does Protodex work with the normal buf CLI? Yes; see the matrix (1.32.2 and newer).

Can I keep using remote plugins (buf.build/protocolbuffers/go)? Remote plugins are hosted by the BSR, not by Protodex. Use local plugins; see the mapping table.

Do I need to regenerate code after migrating? No. Generated code does not depend on the registry. Only generated SDK import paths differ if you consumed BSR-hosted SDKs.

Does it scale horizontally? No. SQLite means one writer; run one replica and use Litestream for durability.

Why does bootstrap complain the database is locked? The server is running. Stop it first.

Why does protodex migrate not migrate my repository? migrate applies database migrations. The repository helper is migrate-buf.

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text:
• Copying, decompiling or deriving from any non-public Buf server code, container images or closed-source protos.
  • Using Buf's name or logos as product branding.
  • Feature parity with every hosted BSR product feature; the target is the registry API the open-source buf CLI uses (no hosted remote plugins, hosted SDKs, or Buf's policy/checks products).

docs.title: Blob garbage collection
docs.text: File contents live in the blob store, shared across commits and modules. Contents nobody references any more are left behind when a module is deleted or when a push stores its blobs and then fails before committing. The blob garbage collector removes them.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
Each run is a mark-and-sweep (internal/gc):

  1. Mark: list the blob store and the blob rows, and read the set of digests that some commit manifest references.
  2. Sweep: every unreferenced blob whose stored object is older than the grace period is claimed, re-checked against the database and only then deleted (the row first, then the object). Blob rows that have no stored object are swept without an age check. A deletion that fails is counted and retried on the next run.

docs.title: Concurrent pushes
docs.text: A push may reuse content that already sits in the store as an old, unreferenced orphan. Writing that blob is a no-op, so its age doesn't change, and the commit that references it is written slightly later. To prevent the collector from deleting the blob in that window, a push pins its blob digests from before the blob writes until its metadata transaction has ended. The collector skips pinned blobs, and a push waits while the collector holds a claim on a digest it needs. Every new reference is created under a pin, so a blob that is claimed and found unreferenced stays unreferenced until it is deleted. The grace period is defence in depth.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Key Env Default gc_interval PROTODEX_GC_INTERVAL 1h Time between runs; 0s disables the collector. The first run happens one interval after start. gc_grace_period PROTODEX_GC_GRACE_PERIOD 24h Minimum age of an unreferenced blob before deletion. gc_dry_run PROTODEX_GC_DRY_RUN false Log and count what would be deleted, without deleting it.

Each run logs a summary (blob gc finished, component gc). In dry-run mode each blob that would be deleted is logged at info level.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text: Metric Type Labels protodex_gc_runs_total counter result (ok/error) Completed runs. protodex_gc_duration_seconds histogram – Run duration. protodex_gc_last_success_timestamp_seconds gauge – Time of the last successful run. protodex_gc_blobs_total counter action Unreferenced blobs by outcome: deleted, dry_run (would be deleted), in_flight (spared: pinned by a push), referenced (spared: referenced again before deletion), failed. protodex_gc_bytes_total counter action (deleted/dry_run) Stored bytes of those blobs.

docs.title: Deployment modes
docs.text:
In SQLite mode the collector runs inside protodex serve. The database's process lock guarantees there is only one server, so the in-process pins (gc.Pins) and an always-leading gc.SingleProcess leader are enough.

A multi-replica Postgres deployment will need two pieces, behind interfaces that already exist:

  • a gc.Leader (for example a Postgres advisory lock), so that only one replica, or a separate worker, collects;
  • a database-backed gc.Leases shared by all replicas, because a push on one replica must be visible to the collector on another.

Collection needs a blob store that can list its contents (blob.Lister). Only the filesystem store implements it so far; S3 listing will arrive with the S3 wiring in serve.

docs.title: Migrating from buf.build
docs.text: Moving a repository to Protodex touches the registry host in buf.yaml, buf.lock and your plugin setup. Generated code is unaffected.

docs.title: 1. Get the modules onto Protodex
docs.text:
• Your own modules: buf registry module create then buf push against the new host (see the quickstart).
  • Public dependencies such as googleapis: mirror them, which imports upstream modules with provenance.

Users and organizations must exist first: create organizations with buf registry organization create (instance admins) and users with protodex owner create; see owners.

docs.title: 2. Rename hosts (protodex migrate-buf)
docs.text:
The helper rewrites buf.build/ to your host in every buf.yaml (deps and module name), lists remote plugins in buf.gen*.yaml, and re-runs buf dep update. It is a dry run unless you pass -apply.

protodex migrate-buf -to registry.example.com .            # preview
protodex migrate-buf -to registry.example.com -apply .     # write + buf dep update
Flag Default -to required Protodex host[:port] -from buf.build host to replace -apply off write files and run buf dep update -skip-dep-update off with -apply, do not run buf -buf buf buf binary

By hand: replace the host in deps: and module name: of buf.yaml, and the module name of v1 buf.yaml.

docs.title: 3. buf.lock
docs.text: Never edit buf.lock by hand. buf dep update regenerates it against the new registry; expect changed name, commit and digest values (commit IDs are assigned by the server that stores them). Commit the new lock file. If a dependency was mirrored, its digests match upstream because the digest is computed from content.

docs.title: 4. Log in
docs.text: buf registry login registry.example.com --token-stdin

docs.title: Remote to local plugin mapping
docs.text:
Protodex does not host plugins. Replace remote:/plugin: buf.build/... entries by local plugins:

Remote plugin Local plugin Pin with buf.build/protocolbuffers/go protoc-gen-go Go: go get -tool google.golang.org/protobuf/cmd/protoc-gen-go@vX buf.build/grpc/go protoc-gen-go-grpc Go: go get -tool google.golang.org/grpc/cmd/protoc-gen-go-grpc@vX buf.build/connectrpc/go protoc-gen-connect-go Go: go get -tool connectrpc.com/connect/cmd/protoc-gen-connect-go@vX buf.build/community/mfridman-go-json protoc-gen-go-json Go: go get -tool github.com/mfridman/protoc-gen-go-json@vX buf.build/grpc-ecosystem/gateway protoc-gen-grpc-gateway Go: go get -tool github.com/grpc-ecosystem/grpc-gateway/v2/protoc-gen-grpc-gateway@vX buf.build/bufbuild/es protoc-gen-es npm: npm i -D -E @bufbuild/protoc-gen-es buf.build/connectrpc/es protoc-gen-connect-es npm: npm i -D -E @connectrpc/protoc-gen-connect-es

With the Go tool directive (Go 1.24+) plugins are pinned in go.mod; run them through go tool:

# buf.gen.yaml
version: v2
plugins:
  - local: ["go", "tool", "protoc-gen-go"]
    out: gen
    opt: paths=source_relative
  - local: ["go", "tool", "protoc-gen-go-grpc"]
    out: gen

For npm, pin exact versions and call the binary from node_modules:

plugins:
  - local: node_modules/.bin/protoc-gen-es
    out: gen
    opt: target=ts

Pick plugin versions that match the ones the remote plugin used (check buf.gen.yaml remote: ...:vX) to keep generated output identical. migrate-buf only reports remote plugins; it never rewrites them.

docs.title: Generated SDKs
docs.text: BSR-hosted SDKs (buf.build/gen/go/..., @buf/... npm packages) are not served by Protodex. Generate code locally (above) and change imports to your own packages; the generated message and wire formats are unchanged, but Go import paths and npm package names differ. Services and clients keep interoperating on the wire.

docs.title: Mirror license review
docs.text:
An upstream is mirrored (listed in mirror.yaml) only after its license has been checked to permit redistribution of the files. protodex mirror run refuses licenses outside the approved list (internal/mirror, AllowedLicenses); adding one requires an entry here first.

Every mirrored module carries the upstream LICENSE file, which satisfies the notice requirements of the licenses below.

Upstream License Checked Redistribution googleapis/googleapis Apache-2.0 2026-11-17, upstream LICENSE at the pinned commit Permitted (Apache-2.0 §4: provide the license text, keep notices) bufbuild/protovalidate Apache-2.0 2026-11-17, upstream LICENSE at v1.2.2 Permitted (same terms) grpc-ecosystem/grpc-gateway BSD-3-Clause 2026-11-17, upstream LICENSE at v2.34.0 ("Copyright (c) 2015, Gengo, Inc.") Permitted (retain the copyright notice and conditions; no endorsement use of the names)

This is an engineering review of the license texts, not legal advice; operators mirroring other upstreams are responsible for their own review. Files are not modified, so no "modified" notices are needed.

docs.title: Mirroring upstream modules
docs.text:
Published modules can depend on Google's protos by mirroring them onto this registry, under the same owner/module path as upstream:

Module Upstream Pin googleapis/googleapis github.com/googleapis/googleapis (google/) commit bufbuild/protovalidate github.com/bufbuild/protovalidate (proto/protovalidate) tag grpc-ecosystem/grpc-gateway github.com/grpc-ecosystem/grpc-gateway (protoc-gen-openapiv2/) tag

A module then names <host>/googleapis/googleapis in the deps of its buf.yaml; buf dep update, buf build and buf push work as usual.

docs.title: Running it
docs.text:
protodex mirror run    -db protodex.db -config mirror.yaml   # import / update
protodex mirror status -db protodex.db                       # provenance

The command opens the database exclusively, like bootstrap and owner, so stop the server first. It needs git and network access to the upstreams. The mirror owners (googleapis, bufbuild, grpc-ecosystem) are created on demand; reserve them beforehand with protodex bootstrap -mirror-owners.

docs.title: mirror.yaml
docs.text:
upstreams:
  - name: googleapis/googleapis    # owner/module here == upstream path
    url: https://github.com/googleapis/googleapis.git
    ref: 82983a28bdca6e289b1e283fa3aa309929509ba4   # tag or full commit hash
    license: Apache-2.0            # SPDX id, must be approved (see below)
    roots: ["."]                   # proto roots; paths are stored relative to them
    include: [google]              # optional: only .proto files under these prefixes
    labels: []                     # extra labels for the imported commit
    deps: []                       # other upstreams of this file this one depends on
  • Pins only. ref is a tag or a full commit hash, never a branch. A commit pin is verified against the commit git resolved.
  • Tags are tags. A non-hash ref is fetched as refs/tags/<ref>, so a branch name can never be used as a pin.
  • Exact content. .proto files (and the upstream LICENSE) are stored byte for byte (.gitattributes eol/filter settings are ignored) at their path relative to the root, so go_package and every other option are unchanged. Other files are not part of a module.
  • Labels. The imported commit gets main (the default label, so an unpinned dependency resolves), the tag for a tag pin, and any labels. Bumping the pin creates a new commit and moves these labels. If the new pin changes only files that are not mirrored, the content is identical: the existing commit is reused (labels move to it) and its provenance keeps naming the first upstream revision that produced this content.
  • Dependencies. deps are imported first; the dependency commit is recorded as an edge of the new commit and folded into its digest. The upstreams above have no inter-dependencies (protovalidate only imports google/protobuf, which buf provides itself).
  • Idempotent. The commit digest is computed from the content. When the latest commit already has that digest, nothing is written; a re-run with unchanged pins is a no-op.

docs.title: Provenance
docs.text: Each mirrored commit stores its upstream URL, the pinned ref, the resolved upstream commit, the license and the import time. protodex mirror status lists them, and the API serves the upstream commit link as Commit.source_control_url (visible with buf registry module commit info).

docs.title: Access
docs.text: Mirror modules are public, so everyone can read them. The permission model (see permissions.md) caps every caller's permission on a mirror owner's modules at read, instance admins and contributor grants included, so pushes, label moves, settings changes and deletes over the API are refused (PermissionDenied). Only protodex mirror run, which writes to the database directly, changes them.

docs.title: Licenses
docs.text: An upstream is only accepted if its SPDX license is in the approved list (Apache-2.0, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, MIT) and each module ships the upstream LICENSE. See mirror-licenses.md for the review of each upstream.

docs.title: Modules and labels
docs.text:
A module lives at <host>/<owner>/<module>; see owners.md for owners. With a database configured, protodex serves buf.registry.module.v1.ModuleService and LabelService, so these work with the stock buf CLI:

buf registry module create registry.example.com/acme/weather --visibility=public
buf registry module info registry.example.com/acme/weather
buf registry module settings update registry.example.com/acme/weather --description=... --default-label-name=trunk
buf registry module deprecate|undeprecate registry.example.com/acme/weather
buf registry module delete registry.example.com/acme/weather
buf registry module label list|info|archive|unarchive registry.example.com/acme/weather[:label]

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Module names: 2-100 characters; lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen. Unique per owner.
  • Visibility defaults to private. Public modules are readable anonymously; private modules only by callers with a permission on them. A private module the caller cannot read is reported as NotFound.
  • Writes need a token. Pushing and label changes need write permission on the module; settings changes (UpdateModules) and deletion need admin; creating needs a member role in one's own namespace or an organization's (or the instance admin role). Mirror owners' modules are read-only over the API (PermissionDenied). Roles, contributor grants and the full matrix are in permissions.md.
  • Default label: main unless set on creation. It is a name only: labels point at commits, so the label itself appears with the first push. It may name a label that does not exist yet, but not an archived one.
  • Labels: 1-250 characters, no whitespace or control characters (v1.2.0, feature/x are fine). A label can only move to a commit of its own module that is not older than its current commit. Moving an archived label unarchives it. The default label cannot be archived. Label ids stay stable when a label moves.
  • Batch RPCs (CreateModules, UpdateModules, DeleteModules, CreateOrUpdateLabels, ArchiveLabels, UnarchiveLabels) are atomic.
  • List RPCs page with page_size (max 250) and an opaque page_token, and order by create or update time (newest first by default). ListLabels excludes archived labels unless archive_filter says otherwise; its resource_ref may name a module, a label or a commit. Commit check status is always reported as DISABLED (no policy checks).

docs.title: Error codes
docs.text:
Condition Code No token on a write Unauthenticated Unknown or hidden owner/module/label/commit NotFound Module name taken AlreadyExists Invalid module or label name InvalidArgument Missing write/admin permission on a readable module, creating in another user's namespace, a mirror owner, read-only role PermissionDenied Moving a label backwards, archiving the default label, archived default label FailedPrecondition

ListLabelHistory returns Unimplemented (label history is not recorded yet). Only module.v1 is served: no captured CLI command uses v1beta1 (see open-questions.md).

docs.title: CLI test
docs.text:
test/clitest drives the real buf CLI against an in-process server over TLS (<127.0.0.1:port>/owner/module names). It skips unless buf is on PATH or PROTODEX_TEST_BUF points at it:

GOBIN=$PWD/bin/tools go install github.com/bufbuild/buf/cmd/buf@v1.57.0
PROTODEX_TEST_BUF=$PWD/bin/tools/buf go test ./test/clitest/ -v

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
Prometheus text format at GET /metrics (unauthenticated; restrict at the network edge).

Metric Type Labels Description protodex_rpc_requests_total counter procedure, code Completed RPCs (code is the Connect code, ok on success). protodex_rpc_duration_seconds histogram procedure, code RPC latency. protodex_upload_bytes_total counter – Request bytes received on UploadService procedures. protodex_store_operation_duration_seconds histogram operation, status Metadata store latency (status = ok/error). protodex_blob_operation_duration_seconds histogram operation, status Blob storage latency. protodex_http_in_flight_requests gauge – HTTP requests being served. protodex_gc_runs_total, protodex_gc_duration_seconds, protodex_gc_last_success_timestamp_seconds, protodex_gc_blobs_total, protodex_gc_bytes_total – – Blob garbage collection; see gc.md. go_*, process_* – – Standard Go/process collectors.

Store and blob code should wrap calls with Observability.Store / Observability.Blob, which record the histogram and a span in one step.

docs.title: Tracing
docs.text: Off by default. Enable with tracing_enabled (PROTODEX_TRACING_ENABLED, -tracing). Spans are exported over OTLP/HTTP to otlp_endpoint (PROTODEX_OTLP_ENDPOINT, -otlp-endpoint, e.g. http://collector:4318); if empty the standard OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_* variables apply. Incoming W3C traceparent headers are honored. Spans: one server span per RPC (named by procedure), plus protodex.store.<op> and protodex.blob.<op>.

docs.title: Access logs
docs.text: One structured line (msg=access) per HTTP request with request_id, method, path, status, bytes_out, duration, remote and, for RPCs, procedure and code. Headers, query strings and bodies are never logged; path is the RPC procedure, a known operational route, or unmatched, so tokens and file contents cannot leak. Trace spans for store/blob errors carry only the error type. X-Request-Id is accepted from clients if it matches [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}; otherwise one is generated. It is echoed in the response header and attached to spans.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text: deploy/grafana/protodex.json — import into Grafana (Prometheus datasource variable DS_PROMETHEUS).

docs.title: State to protect
docs.text:
• the SQLite database (db_path, plus -wal/-shm files while running);
  • the blob directory (blob_dir, default <db_path>.blobs).

Both are needed: the database references blobs by digest. Keep them on a local block volume, never NFS/EFS (SQLite corruption risk).

docs.title: Backup and restore
docs.text:
• Kubernetes (Helm): Litestream replicates the database to S3 and an init container restores it onto an empty volume. Follow the Restore drill in the chart README regularly.
  • Compose / bare metal: stop the server (or snapshot the volume) and copy the database and blob directory together; alternatively run sqlite3 protodex.db ".backup backup.db" against the live database and copy the blobs after the database so that every referenced blob exists. To restore, stop protodex, put both back, start it. Blobs without a database row are removed by garbage collection after the grace period; a database row without a blob is a corrupt backup.

Test restores before you need them.

docs.title: Upgrades
docs.text:
1. Read the release notes.
  2. Back up (above).
  3. Stop the server: migrate needs the exclusive database lock.
  4. Run protodex migrate when the release notes say the schema changed (compose: docker compose run --rm --no-deps protodex migrate). Roll back one step with migrate down.
  5. Start the new image/chart. Helm uses Recreate, so expect a short downtime.

Protodex is a single-writer system; there is no rolling upgrade.

docs.title: Monitoring
docs.text: /healthz, /readyz, Prometheus /metrics and the Grafana dashboard are covered in observability. /metrics is unauthenticated: restrict it at the network edge.

docs.title: Owners: users, the instance organization and mirror owners
docs.text:
Every module lives under an owner: <host>/<owner>/<module>. Protodex uses a single-organization model: an instance normally has one organization (the company or team running it) plus its users. The owners table still holds any number of owners, so extra organizations (teams, namespaces) and mirror owners can coexist.

  • Users authenticate with tokens and can own modules. Names: 1-32 characters. Each user has an instance role (viewer, member or admin; see permissions.md).
  • Organizations own shared modules. Names: 1-48 characters.
  • Mirror owners are organizations that reserve an upstream owner name such as googleapis or bufbuild, so mirrored modules keep their upstream path (see ADR 0001). A mirror owner keeps its name: it cannot be renamed.

All names use lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, start with a letter and do not end with a hyphen. Users, organizations and mirror owners share one namespace: a name can be used by only one owner, so a local owner can never shadow a mirror.

Owner IDs never change. Renaming a user or organization keeps its modules and tokens; the old name becomes free (there is no redirect).

docs.title: Bootstrap
docs.text:
protodex bootstrap -db protodex.db -user admin -org acme -mirror-owners googleapis,bufbuild

Creates the first user, an instance admin (printing its token once), the instance organization and the mirror owners. Rerunning is safe: existing owners of the same kind are left alone, and a name held by another kind of owner is an error.

Flag Environment Meaning -db PROTODEX_DB_PATH SQLite database -user PROTODEX_BOOTSTRAP_USER first user (default admin) -org PROTODEX_BOOTSTRAP_ORG instance organization (optional) -mirror-owners PROTODEX_MIRROR_OWNERS comma-separated reserved mirror owners – PROTODEX_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN use this token instead of generating one

docs.title: Managing owners
docs.text:
protodex owner create -db protodex.db user alice bob   # prints a token per user
protodex owner create -db protodex.db -role viewer user auditor
protodex owner role   -db protodex.db alice admin       # viewer, member or admin
protodex owner create -db protodex.db org platform
protodex owner create -db protodex.db mirror grpc-ecosystem
protodex owner list   -db protodex.db
protodex owner rename -db protodex.db platform platform-team

create is all-or-nothing: if one name is taken, none are created. The commands take the database's exclusive lock, so run them while the server is stopped.

docs.title: API
docs.text:
With a database configured, the server answers:

RPC Behaviour OwnerService.GetOwners Resolves owner names/IDs to users or organizations; any unknown owner is NotFound. UserService.GetUsers, GetCurrentUser, ListUsers GetCurrentUser needs a token. Users are reported as standard and active; admins with instance role ADMIN, members and viewers as MEMBER. ListUsers filters on has_roles. OrganizationService.GetOrganizations, ListOrganizations Mirror owners are listed as organizations.

Reads work anonymously. List RPCs page with page_size (max 250) and an opaque page_token. Filtering by organization membership (ListUsers organization_refs, ListOrganizations user_refs) is not modeled yet and returns Unimplemented.

docs.title: Administration over the API
docs.text:
Instance admins can manage owners with the API, which is what buf registry organization create|update|delete uses:

RPC Behaviour OrganizationService.CreateOrganizations, UserService.CreateUsers Create owners atomically, with optional description and URL. A taken name is AlreadyExists, an invalid one InvalidArgument. New users are members without a token: issue one with protodex owner or have them log in through OIDC. OrganizationService.UpdateOrganizations, UserService.UpdateUsers Change description and URL. Mirror owners cannot be updated. OrganizationService.DeleteOrganizations, UserService.DeleteUsers Delete owners atomically, with their tokens and contributor grants. Refused (FailedPrecondition) while the owner still owns modules, for mirror owners and for yourself.

Not modeled, so they return Unimplemented: user types other than standard, user state other than active, verification status, organization visibility other than public, and GetOrganizationSettings / UpdateOrganizationSettings. Run protodex migrate after upgrading (migration 9 adds the description and URL columns).

docs.title: Permissions: roles, visibility and contributors
docs.text:
Protodex decides every request in two layers:

  1. Procedure policy (an interceptor, internal/server/permissions.go). Every RPC is listed in one table as anonymous, authenticated, write or admin. Procedures that are not listed are denied, and a test checks that the table covers every vendored registry RPC.
  2. Resource checks in the handlers: the caller's permission on each module (or owner, for creation) the request touches.

docs.title: Instance roles
docs.text:
Every user has one instance role:

Role Meaning viewer (read-only) Reads public modules, organization modules and their own namespace. Cannot create, push, label, change or delete anything, unless a module grants them more (see contributors). member Full access to their own namespace and to organization namespaces (single-organization model). Cannot read or change other users' private modules. The default for new users. admin Full access to every module of every owner, except mirror modules. Required for the admin-only RPCs (organization and user management, see owners.md).

Roles come from:

  • protodex bootstrap: the first user is an admin.
  • protodex owner create [-role viewer|member|admin] user NAME... (default member) and protodex owner role USER ROLE.
  • OIDC login: the role derived from the IdP's groups (group_roles, default_role; see the README) replaces the user's role on every login, so for OIDC users the IdP is the source of truth.

protodex owner list shows each user's role. Over the API, UserService reports admins as USER_INSTANCE_ROLE_ADMIN and members and viewers as USER_INSTANCE_ROLE_MEMBER (the API has no read-only role), and ListUsers can filter on has_roles.

Upgrading: migration 7 makes every existing user a member, which keeps the access they had before roles were enforced. Promote your administrators afterwards with protodex owner role NAME admin.

docs.title: Module visibility
docs.text:
• Public modules are readable by anyone, including anonymous callers.
  • Private modules (the default) are readable only by callers with a permission on them (below).
  • A module the caller cannot read is reported as NotFound, never PermissionDenied, so its existence does not leak. This also holds for dependencies: GraphService.GetGraph and FileDescriptorSetService.GetFileDescriptorSet of a readable module fail with NotFound when a transitive dependency is not readable, and a push may only depend on commits the pusher can read. DownloadService.Download returns a commit's own files only, so a public module stays downloadable even if it depends on a private one.

docs.title: Module permissions
docs.text:
A caller's permission on a module is the highest of:

Source Permission Module is public read Instance admin admin member on their own namespace or an organization's admin viewer on their own namespace or an organization's read Contributor grant on the module read, write or admin

…capped at read for modules of mirror owners: those are managed by mirroring and are read-only over the API for everyone, admins included.

What each permission allows:

Action Needs Get/list the module, its commits, labels, resources, files, graph, descriptors read Push (UploadService.Upload), create/move/archive/unarchive labels write Change settings (UpdateModules: visibility, description, URL, default label, deprecation) and delete admin Create a module under an owner member on their own namespace or an organization, or instance admin; never under a mirror owner Manage own tokens (TokenService), GetCurrentUser any authenticated user

Write procedures are closed to viewers at the interceptor unless they hold at least one write or admin grant; the handler then checks the grant for the specific module.

docs.title: Contributors
docs.text:
A contributor grant gives one user a role on one module: read, write or admin. Grants only add access; they never reduce what a user's instance role already allows. They are removed with the module or the user. Mirror modules take no grants.

protodex contributor add    -db protodex.db acme/weather alice write
protodex contributor list   -db protodex.db acme/weather
protodex contributor remove -db protodex.db acme/weather alice

Like protodex owner, these commands take the database's exclusive lock, so run them while the server is stopped.

The buf CLI has no commands for roles or contributors, so protodex does not serve an API for them (no iam/v1 permission or contributor services are vendored).

docs.title: Error codes
docs.text: Condition Code No token on a non-anonymous RPC Unauthenticated Module (or dependency) not readable by the caller NotFound Readable module, but missing write/admin permission; any write to a mirror module; creating under another user's or a mirror owner's namespace; a viewer calling a write RPC without any write grant; a non-admin calling an admin RPC PermissionDenied

docs.title: Push and commits
docs.text:
With a database configured, protodex serves buf.registry.module.v1.UploadService and CommitService, so buf push works with the stock CLI:

buf push                 # in a directory whose buf.yaml names registry.example.com/acme/weather
buf push --label=v1
buf registry module commit info registry.example.com/acme/weather:<commit>

The module must exist (buf registry module create); push does not create it.

docs.title: How a push is stored
docs.text:
• File contents go to the blob store (blob_dir, default <db_path>.blobs; env PROTODEX_BLOB_DIR), keyed by SHA-256, so identical files are stored once across commits and modules. S3 is not wired into serve yet. Blobs that end up unreferenced (deleted modules, failed pushes) are removed by garbage collection.
  • Only module files are kept: *.proto, LICENSE, and the first of buf.md, README.md, README.markdown. Other files (buf.yaml, ...) are ignored.
  • Commit, manifest, dependency edges and label moves are written in one database transaction. Concurrent pushes are serialised; a label always ends on the newest commit.
  • The commit ID is a server-assigned 32-character dashless UUID. The server computes the commit's b5 digest itself (see internal/b5) from the files and the digests of the dependency commits; it matches what the CLI computes.
  • Pushing content identical to the module's latest commit returns that commit (idempotent) and only moves labels. Pushing older content again creates a new commit with the same digest, so labels never move backwards.
  • Labels: the --label values, or the module's default label. Archived labels are unarchived by a push.
  • Dependencies (dep_commit_ids) must be commits on this server that the caller can read; they are recorded as edges and folded into the digest. The CLI sends transitive dependencies too, and all of them are recorded.
  • Pushed source_control_url is accepted but not stored yet.

docs.title: Gating breaking changes in CI
docs.text:
The server does not reject breaking pushes (see ADR 0002). Check in CI before buf push, comparing against the module's latest commit on the registry:

buf breaking --against registry.example.com/acme/weather
buf breaking --against registry.example.com/acme/weather:v1   # a specific label

docs.title: Limits and errors
docs.text:
max_push_files (default 5000) and max_push_file_bytes (default 10 MiB) bound a module; the request as a whole is bounded by max_request_bytes.

Condition Code No token Unauthenticated Unknown or hidden module, label id or dependency commit NotFound Writing another user's namespace or a mirror owner PermissionDenied Too many or too large files, duplicate paths, no module files, bad label name, same module twice, self- or duplicate-module dependency InvalidArgument

CommitService.ListCommits of a label or commit returns just that commit; id_query is a case-insensitive substring match.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
Modules uploaded together in one request are not made dependencies of each other: only dep_commit_ids become edges (detecting local imports would need parsing the files).

buf push of a module with dependencies also calls GraphService and DownloadService; both are served now (see reads.md), so the CLI can push such modules once buf dep update has written buf.lock.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: You need Docker with Compose (or a Kubernetes cluster with Helm) and a buf CLI of version 1.32.2 or newer (see compatibility).

docs.title: Docker Compose
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/MarijnKoesen/protodex && cd protodex
cp deploy/.env.example deploy/.env      # optional; change the secrets

# 1. Create the admin user, an organization and the first token.
#    The server must not be running: bootstrap takes the database lock.
docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yaml run --rm --no-deps protodex \
  bootstrap -org acme
# The token is printed ONCE. Save it.

# 2. Start the stack (protodex + SeaweedFS + SQLite volume).
docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yaml up -d --build
curl -fsS http://localhost:8080/healthz   # -> ok

bootstrap prints the admin token only once; to choose it yourself, set PROTODEX_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN. More settings are in deploy/README.md.

docs.title: Kubernetes (Helm)
docs.text:
helm install protodex oci://ghcr.io/marijnkoesen/charts/protodex \
  --version X.Y.Z -n protodex --create-namespace -f my-values.yaml

Run protodex bootstrap -org acme once inside the pod before first use (scale to zero first, or run it as a Job on the same volume, because it needs the database lock). Values, ingress, Litestream backups and the restore drill are described in the chart README.

docs.title: Push your first module
docs.text:
buf only speaks TLS to registries, including localhost, while protodex serves plain HTTP (h2c). Pointing buf straight at localhost:8080 fails with the server hosted at that remote is unavailable. Put a TLS proxy in front, also locally. For example, with Caddy:

# Serves https://localhost:8443 with a certificate from Caddy's local CA.
# On first run Caddy asks for your password to add that CA to the system
# trust store, which buf uses (Go ignores SSL_CERT_FILE on macOS).
caddy reverse-proxy --from localhost:8443 --to localhost:8080

Below, localhost:8443 is the proxy.

# Log in with the token printed by bootstrap.
buf registry login localhost:8443 --token-stdin <<<"$TOKEN"

# Create a module and push.
mkdir hello && cd hello
cat > buf.yaml <<'YAML'
version: v2
modules:
  - path: proto
    name: localhost:8443/acme/hello
YAML
mkdir proto && echo 'syntax = "proto3"; package hello.v1; message Ping {}' > proto/ping.proto
buf registry module create localhost:8443/acme/hello --visibility private
buf push
buf registry module label info localhost:8443/acme/hello:main   # shows the commit `main` points to

Consume it from another repository. buf needs at least one .proto file of its own there, otherwise buf dep update fails with had no .proto files:

mkdir app && cd app
cat > buf.yaml <<'YAML'
version: v2
modules:
  - path: proto
deps:
  - localhost:8443/acme/hello
YAML
mkdir proto && cat > proto/app.proto <<'PROTO'
syntax = "proto3";
package app.v1;
import "ping.proto";
message Request { hello.v1.Ping ping = 1; }
PROTO
buf dep update   # writes buf.lock
buf build

Next: migrating an existing repository.

docs.title: Reading modules: download, resources, graph, descriptor sets
docs.text:
With a database and blob store configured, protodex serves the read side of buf.registry.module.v1, so the stock CLI can consume pushed modules:

buf build registry.example.com/acme/weather            # default label
buf build registry.example.com/acme/weather:v1         # a label
buf build registry.example.com/acme/weather:<commit>   # a commit
buf export registry.example.com/acme/weather -o out/
buf dep update                                          # with deps on this host in buf.yaml

buf build/buf export of a remote module call CommitService/GetCommits, GraphService/GetGraph, ModuleService/GetModules, OwnerService/GetOwners and, unless the commit is in the CLI's cache, DownloadService/Download (observed with buf 1.57.0, test/clitest). They do not call FileDescriptorSetService; it is for API clients that want compiled descriptors.

docs.title: Resolving references
docs.text:
All read services resolve a ResourceRef the same way (as CommitService):

Reference Resolves to owner/module the commit of the module's default label owner/module + label_name that label's commit owner/module + ref the commit with that id in the module, else the label with that name id the commit, label or module with that id (tried in that order)

So :main, :<label> and :<commit-id> select identical content when they name the same commit. A module without commits (no default label yet) is NotFound for Download, Graph and FileDescriptorSet; GetResources returns the module itself. Digest references (b5:...) are not a ResourceRef form and are not accepted.

docs.title: Services
docs.text:
• DownloadService.Download returns the files of each resolved commit (.proto, LICENSE, documentation). file_types and paths narrow the result; a path also selects the files below it (foo/bar matches foo/bar/baz.proto). A path matching no file (after the type filter) is NotFound unless paths_allow_not_exist is set.
  • ResourceService.GetResources returns, per reference, the module, label or commit it names.
  • GraphService.GetGraph returns the resolved commits, their transitive dependency commits (as recorded at push time) and the edges between them. Commits are topologically ordered (a commit precedes its dependencies); diamonds appear once, and different commits of one module are all returned so the client (buf dep update) picks the version. A cycle in stored data is FailedPrecondition. Only dependencies on this registry exist (see open-questions.md).
  • FileDescriptorSetService.GetFileDescriptorSet compiles the commit and its dependency commits (with bufbuild/protocompile; well-known types are built in) and returns the files in topological order. exclude_imports, include_source_code_info and include_source_retention_options are honoured; include_types/exclude_types return Unimplemented. A commit that does not compile is FailedPrecondition. Results are cached in memory (LRU, 64 MiB) by commit digest and options: a b5 digest pins the files and the dependency digests, so it pins the whole input.

docs.title: Access
docs.text: Every read goes through the same visibility check as ModuleService (canRead in internal/server/modules.go): public modules are readable anonymously, private ones only by callers with access, and a hidden module, label or commit is reported as NotFound. Dependencies reached through the graph are checked too. When the permissions model (issue #26) lands, it replaces that one function. The cache is consulted only after the check.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Condition Code Unknown or hidden module, label or commit; module without commits; missing path NotFound Module does not compile, or two modules of the graph share a path FailedPrecondition Type filters; cross-registry dependency Unimplemented

docs.title: Security review checklist
docs.text: Run before each release (and for changes touching auth, parsing or storage).

docs.title: Code
docs.text:
• [ ] New RPCs are in the policy table (internal/server/permissions.go) and have a permission test.
  • [ ] Every request-controlled size or count is bounded (see docs/threat-model.md).
  • [ ] No secret (token, client secret) is logged or returned after creation.
  • [ ] Parsers of untrusted input have a fuzz target; run make fuzz (or go test -fuzz per target, ≥ 1 min each).
  • [ ] go vet ./..., golangci-lint run and govulncheck ./... are clean.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
• [ ] Dependabot PRs for Go modules, GitHub Actions and Docker are merged or consciously deferred.
  • [ ] govulncheck shows no reachable vulnerabilities.

docs.title: Container and deployment
docs.text:
• [ ] Image is distroless static, digest pinned, runs as UID 65532 (Dockerfile).
  • [ ] Helm/compose: non-root, read-only root filesystem, dropped capabilities, NetworkPolicy enabled where supported.
  • [ ] TLS terminates at the proxy; rate_limit.trust_forwarded_for is set only if the proxy sets X-Forwarded-For.
  • [ ] /metrics is not exposed publicly.

docs.title: Process
docs.text:
• [ ] SECURITY.md points to a working private reporting channel (GitHub private vulnerability reporting enabled in repository settings).
  • [ ] Threat model updated.
  • [ ] Before 1.0: external penetration test completed and findings triaged.

docs.title: Security notes
docs.text:
• TLS: Protodex speaks plain HTTP/h2c. Terminate TLS at a reverse proxy or ingress; buf refuses non-TLS registries other than localhost. Set rate_limit.trust_forwarded_for only if your proxy sets X-Forwarded-For.
  • Tokens: bearer tokens are shown once and stored hashed. Treat the bootstrap token like a root credential; rotate by creating a new token and deleting the old one. Roles and visibility are described in permissions.
  • OIDC: users are keyed by the stable (issuer, subject) pair, never by e-mail.
  • Network exposure: do not expose /metrics publicly. The compose file binds to 127.0.0.1 by default.
  • Container: distroless, non-root (65532), read-only root filesystem. Images and charts are cosign-signed; verification steps are in the deploy README.
  • Supply chain / limits: push size limits and rate limits bound abuse; see the threat model and the release checklist.

Report vulnerabilities privately as described in SECURITY.md.

docs.title: Threat model
docs.text: Scope: a single protodex serve process (SQLite metadata, filesystem or S3 blobs) behind a TLS-terminating reverse proxy, used through buf and the web UI.

docs.title: Assets
docs.text:
• Schema contents of private modules; token secrets; OIDC client secret.
  • Integrity of commits and their b5 digests (consumers pin them).
  • Availability of the registry and its storage.

docs.title: Trust boundaries
docs.text: Boundary Notes Internet/clients → proxy → protodex TLS is terminated by the proxy; protodex speaks plain HTTP/h2c. Anonymous vs. authenticated Anonymous callers may read public modules only (docs/permissions.md). protodex → blob store / IdP Credentials come from the environment; the IdP is trusted for identity and groups.

docs.title: Threats and mitigations
docs.text: Threat Mitigation Status Token brute force / credential stuffing 256-bit random secrets, stored hashed, constant-time compare; per-IP and per-token rate limits done Request flooding / scraping of anonymous reads Per-IP token bucket on every request (rate_limit.ip_*) done Oversized or many-file pushes max_request_bytes, max_push_files, max_push_file_bytes, max_push_bytes done Slowloris / idle connections ReadHeaderTimeout, IdleTimeout, MaxHeaderBytes done Malicious paths in pushed files (traversal) Paths must be clean, relative, slash-separated; blobs are content-addressed, never named by clients done Digest/manifest parser bugs Go fuzz targets FuzzDigest, FuzzBytes in internal/b5 done Privilege escalation across modules/owners Role + visibility + contributor checks in the interceptor chain; tests in internal/server/permissions_test.go done Spoofed client IP to evade limits X-Forwarded-For ignored unless rate_limit.trust_forwarded_for; then only the last (proxy-appended) entry is used done Storage exhaustion by one owner Per-push byte cap only; no per-owner storage quota yet open Distributed floods Limits are per client and per process; use proxy/WAF limits for volumetric attacks out of scope Compromised dependency / image Dependabot, digest-pinned distroless nonroot image, signed releases see checklist

docs.title: Residual risks / non-goals
docs.text:
• Rate limiter state is in memory and per replica; restarts reset it.
  • Clients behind one NAT/proxy share an IP bucket; tune rate_limit.ip_rate.
  • No external penetration test has been done; schedule one before 1.0.

docs.title: Web UI
docs.text:
protodex serve serves a small single-page app at / (assets under /ui/). It is plain ES modules with no build step, embedded in the binary (internal/webui), and talks only to the public Connect API using the Connect JSON protocol — there are no private endpoints.

Pages: module list (filter by owner), module overview, commit history, labels, a proto/file browser (by label or commit), access-token management (list, create, delete; the secret is shown once) and sign-in.

  • Sign-in: paste a personal access token (kept in sessionStorage, i.e. for the tab only). With OIDC enabled, "sign in with OIDC" (/auth/login) issues a token to paste. A UI-native OIDC session is not implemented.
  • Mirror provenance: a commit's source_control_url is shown as "source" on the overview and file pages.
  • Accessibility / theme: skip link, landmarks, labelled controls, focus outlines, prefers-color-scheme with a manual toggle.
  • All API data is rendered with textContent; a strict CSP (no inline script) is set.

docs.title: End-to-end tests
docs.text:
Playwright tests live in e2e/ and run in CI (e2e job):

make build
cd e2e && npm ci && npx playwright install chromium
E2E_TOKEN="pdx_$(head -c 32 /dev/urandom | base64 | tr '+/' '-_' | tr -d '=\n')" npx playwright test

docs.title: ADR 0001: Naming and addressing
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-17

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The project began under the placeholder name "Openbuf" with module path example.com/openbuf. "Buf" is a trademark of Buf Technologies, Inc., and the project is an independent clean-room implementation that is not affiliated with them (see README non-goals). Keeping "buf" in the product name risks trademark problems, so we renamed before code accumulated.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Item Value Project / binary name protodex Go module path github.com/marijnkoesen/protodex Container image ghcr.io/marijnkoesen/protodex Helm chart OCI: oci://ghcr.io/marijnkoesen/charts/protodex (chart name protodex) Domain None yet. The server host is always configuration, never hard-coded.

The module path, image and chart live under the GitHub owner so they need no domain purchase. They are chosen publication locations; nothing is published there yet. If the project moves to an organisation or a custom domain, the module path changes in a single mechanical PR. The GitHub repository itself must be renamed from openbuf to protodex (GitHub redirects the old name).

docs.title: Mirror addressing
docs.text:
Mirrored modules keep their upstream owner/module path under our host:

<host>/googleapis/googleapis   (mirrors buf.build/googleapis/googleapis)

Migrating a consumer from buf.build is therefore a host rename in buf.yaml dependencies (deps:) and buf.lock, with no path rewriting, provided the mirror preserves upstream commit IDs, content digests and dependency references, because buf.lock pins those, not just names. If a mirror cannot guarantee that, consumers must regenerate buf.lock (buf dep update) after switching hosts. Locally created modules use the same <host>/<owner>/<module> form; mirrored owners are reserved so a local owner cannot shadow an upstream one.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• One consistent name across code, image and chart.
  • A later move to an organisation or domain is cheap.

docs.title: ADR 0002: Policy APIs (policy/v1) and breaking-change gates
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted (deferred; revisit on the triggers below)
  • Date: 2026-11-17

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
Issue #33 asks us to evaluate demand for a policy/v1 API and server-side breaking-change checks on push, and to build them only if needed. Remote plugins and plugin APIs are out of scope regardless.

What exists today:

  • Protodex serves the vendored module/v1, owner/v1 and iam/v1 services, which are what the stock buf CLI needs to push and pull (see push.md).
  • proto/ does not contain policy/v1. The vendored subset is pinned to one registry-proto commit and only changes by copying files from upstream (see proto/README.md). Nothing in the current repository, plan or behaviour spec depends on it.
  • The dependencies #26 (roles, visibility, contributors) and #12 are done, so per-module authorization is available if policy is ever enforced.

docs.title: Evaluation
docs.text:
• Client-side checks already cover the main case. buf breaking runs in CI against a registry module or git ref using the module read services protodex already serves (see reads.md). Teams get breaking-change gating without any server feature.
  • No demand signal. No issue, user report or plan item asks for server-enforced policy. The issue itself is labelled "Later, optional".
  • Cost and risk are high. A server-side gate needs a breaking-change engine (rule sets, FILE/PACKAGE/WIRE categories, per-module configuration), and every new rule is a compatibility and clean-room obligation. A wrong rejection blocks pushes, which makes false positives expensive.
  • Wire contract is unsettled. policy/v1 would have to be vendored from upstream or written fresh. A fresh proto risks diverging from what buf expects, which defeats the wire-compatibility goal.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Do not implement policy/v1 or server-side breaking-change gates now. Keep UploadService unchanged. Document buf breaking against the registry in CI as the supported way to gate breaking changes; see push.md.

docs.title: Revisit when
docs.text:
Reopen this ADR (and file a scoped implementation issue) if any of these hold:

  1. Multiple users ask for push-time enforcement that cannot be done in CI, for example because pushes come from untrusted or uncontrolled clients.
  2. A buf CLI feature we want to support requires policy/v1 endpoints.
  3. A stable upstream policy/v1 is available to vendor under the existing process.

A first implementation should then be limited to a per-module opt-in check in UploadService that rejects a push with failed_precondition and reuses the existing roles from permissions.md.

docs.title: Behaviour spec
docs.text: Written from observation of the real buf CLI only (clean-room). Fill in after running make capture; see rpc-matrix.md.

docs.title: To document from captures
docs.text:
• Digests: algorithm/type (b4/b5), where the CLI sends and verifies them.
  • Commit IDs: format (dashless UUID vs. legacy), per CLI version.
  • Labels: creation on push, default label, archive/unarchive semantics.
  • v1 vs v1beta1: which service versions each CLI version calls.

docs.title: Observed against protodex (buf 1.57.0, test/clitest)
docs.text:
• The CLI accepts 127.0.0.1:<port>/<owner>/<module> remotes over TLS (trusting the server via SSL_CERT_FILE); BUF_TOKEN is sent as a bearer token.
  • registry module create on an existing name reports a module named "<remote>/<owner>/<module>" already exists, so the CLI maps AlreadyExists itself.
  • registry module info --format=json prints id, owner, name, create time, state and default label name, but not visibility or description.
  • registry module label list on a module without commits prints nothing.
  • buf build <remote> and buf export <remote> (by module, :label or :commit) call CommitService/GetCommits, GraphService/GetGraph, ModuleService/GetModules, OwnerService/GetOwners and, for commits not yet in BUF_CACHE_DIR, DownloadService/Download; GetGraph is called even for a module without dependencies. FileDescriptorSetService is not called.

docs.title: Open compatibility questions
docs.text:
Status of each assumption from the plan (sections 3, 6, 10), with evidence. Evidence comes from running the real buf CLI (1.32.0, 1.40.0 and, partly, 1.50.0/1.55.0) through the capture harness (test/capture) against buf.build, run natively (no Docker) with /etc/hosts pointing buf.build at the proxy, plus direct CLI runs and string inspection of the release binaries. Raw recordings are git-ignored and not committed.

Legend: VERIFIED = observed; PARTIAL = observed in part; UNVERIFIED = could not be tested yet, with the test that will settle it.

docs.title: Limits of this run
docs.text:
• There is no protodex server yet, so nothing was tested against a protodex host. Questions 1 and 2 need one (see "How to settle").
  • No BUF_TOKEN/PUSH_MODULE was available, so no push was recorded.
  • 1.50.0 and 1.55.0 runs were mostly 502s or empty from the proxy path (upstream flakiness / timeouts), so the per-RPC matrix is only trustworthy for 1.32.0 and 1.40.0. Re-run make capture with Docker to fill it in.

docs.title: 1. Cross-registry dependencies on push - UNVERIFIED
docs.text: No evidence either way. The claim (from protos.rip) is that all transitive deps must live on the module's own host. The buf.lock format supports it structurally: each dep is name: <host>/<owner>/<module> + commit + digest, so a lock can mention foreign hosts, but whether the server rejects it is server behaviour. Scope decision: assume same-host-only (the safe case). The mirror design in ADR 0001 already keeps deps on our host. Do not implement cross-host resolution; revisit only if a test shows the CLI sends such deps. How to settle: once protodex accepts UploadService/Upload, push a module whose buf.lock references buf.build/... and record the response.

docs.title: 2. remote: plugins with deps from our host - PARTIAL
docs.text: buf generate with remote: buf.build/protocolbuffers/go calls buf.alpha.registry.v1alpha1.CodeGenerationService/GenerateCode on the plugin's host (observed in 1.32.0 and 1.40.0; response 400 with a dummy token/unauthenticated). The host comes from the plugin reference, not from the module's deps, so the call goes to buf.build regardless of where the module lives. Whether buf.build accepts an image whose deps came from another host was not tested (400 was returned before reaching that point). Scope decision: protodex does not implement CodeGenerationService; remote plugins keep working only as long as the plugin host (buf.build) is reachable by the client and accepts the image. Treat as out of scope for MVP.

docs.title: 3. Minimum CLI version and v1 vs v1beta1 - PARTIAL
docs.text:
• 1.32.0 and 1.40.0 both use buf.registry.module.v1 for buf dep update: CommitService/GetCommits, GraphService/GetGraph (x2), DownloadService/Download, ModuleService/GetModules. 1.40.0 also uses LabelService/ListLabels for buf registry label list.
  • buf registry module info does not exist in 1.32.0 (unknown subcommand); it is present in 1.40.0+.
  • No v1beta1 call was observed in any recorded scenario. The binaries (1.32.0 and 1.55.0) contain client stubs for both buf.registry.module.v1 and v1beta1 (Commit, Download, Graph, Label, Module, Upload), 1.55.0 additionally v1.ResourceService and buf.registry.plugin.v1beta1.*, buf.registry.owner.v1.*. Which command triggers v1beta1 is not established.
  • 1.32.0 is the oldest version that calls buf.registry.module.v1 (buf.lock v2 / version: v2 config accepted, and dep update works), consistent with the target of >= 1.32. Scope decision: keep minimum CLI = 1.32.0; implement module.v1 services first (Commit, Graph, Download, Module, Label, Upload). Defer v1beta1 until a capture shows a command that needs it.

docs.title: 4. Host remap / mirror setting - VERIFIED (none found)
docs.text: buf --help-tree (1.55.0) shows no mirror/remap command, and the binary's env vars are only BUF_TOKEN, BUF_CACHE_DIR, BUF_ALPHA/BETA_SUPPRESS_WARNINGS, BUF_INPUT_*, BUF_BETA_COPY_FILES_TO_MEMORY, BUF_REGISTRATION_CONFLICT and testing-only BUF_TESTING_PUBLIC_REGISTRY / BUF_TESTING_LEGACY_FEDERATION_REGISTRY. The registry host is taken from the module name, so consumers must rename the host in buf.yaml/buf.lock (matches ADR 0001). The harness itself works by DNS override plus a trusted cert (SSL_CERT_FILE), which is a test technique, not a supported setting. The CLI dials port 443.

docs.title: 5. Commit IDs and digests - PARTIAL
docs.text:
Both 1.32.0 and 1.55.0 wrote an identical buf.lock for buf.build/bufbuild/protovalidate:

version: v2
deps:
  - name: buf.build/bufbuild/protovalidate
    commit: 511051f7f4374c3ca873b53ae68a9288
    digest: b5:a4a2d4d808a25984cced60769c822c5d496ef0b740f56ac0c9e6b97aaa25b86a9332a00ffd74e0cd202be29e91bd3edfb0bf2ba4dacfe48ff2d8217f9986e3c8
    # b5: + 128 hex chars = 64-byte digest. The hash function is not
    # established by observation here (an external review reports SHAKE256,
    # not SHA-512; unconfirmed, clean-room rules forbid reading CLI source).
  • Commit ID: 32 lowercase hex chars (dashless UUID).
  • Digest type: b5 for v2 locks. b4 was not observed here (it appears in legacy v1 locks; not produced by these versions).
  • Whether the CLI validates the digest on dep update/build, and what it checks on push, was not tested (needs a push or a tampered mirror). Scope decision: mirrors must preserve upstream commit IDs and b5 digests (as in ADR 0001). Computing b5 digests ourselves for locally pushed modules is deferred: the digest above has no reproducible inputs (the module's file set is not recorded), so it is not yet a usable test vector. Mirrors simply pass digests through unchanged.

docs.title: 6. Non-buf.registry.* endpoints - VERIFIED for observed commands
docs.text:
Observed non-buf.registry.* calls: - buf registry login -> buf.alpha.registry.v1alpha1.AuthnService/GetCurrentUser (401 with a dummy token). - buf generate with remote plugins -> buf.alpha.registry.v1alpha1.CodeGenerationService/GenerateCode.

dep update, build, label list and module info used only buf.registry.module.v1. No well-known paths were requested. Scope decision: MVP must serve AuthnService/GetCurrentUser (v1alpha1) for buf registry login to succeed against protodex, in addition to module.v1. Remote-plugin codegen stays out of scope (see 2).

docs.title: Plan impact
docs.text: docs/plan.html is unchanged: no assumption was found wrong, but the login dependency on the v1alpha1 AuthnService (6) should be added to the plan's API list if it is not there yet.

docs.title: How to settle the open items
docs.text:
1. Re-run make capture with Docker on a networked machine; include BUF_TOKEN/PUSH_MODULE to record push (questions 3, 5).
  2. When protodex serves module.v1, push a module with a foreign-host dep (1) and run buf generate with a remote: plugin against it (2).
